import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 401

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/401](https://www.erdosproblems.com/401)
- [ErGr80] Erdős, P. and Graham, R., *Old and new problems and results in combinatorial number
  theory*. Monographies de L'Enseignement Mathematique (1980).
-/

open Filter

namespace Erdos401

/--
Is there some function $f(r)$ such that $f(r)\to \infty$ as $r\to\infty$, such that, for
infinitely many $n$, there exist $a_1,a_2$ with
$$a_1+a_2> n+f(r)\log n$$
such that $a_1!a_2! \mid n!2^n3^n\cdots p_r^n$?

It is ambiguous in [ErGr80] what the intended quantifiers are on the variables (they write 'is
it true that we can find $a_1+a_2>n+f(r)\log n$...'). Comparing to previous problems such as
[728] and [729] it seems most likely that they intended to ask the formulation in the problem
statement.

The answer is yes: Barreto and Leeham have used ChatGPT to provide a proof of the stated problem
(in fact essentially the same construction as their solution to [729]).
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11, formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/1d7b3f00780b85ed0462e79a1cd5650ee9055655/src/v4.29.1/ErdosProblems/Erdos401.lean"]
theorem erdos_401 : answer(True) ↔
    ∃ f : ℕ → ℝ, Tendsto f atTop atTop ∧
      ∀ (r : ℕ) (hr : 1 ≤ r),
        {n : ℕ | ∃ a₁ a₂ : ℕ, 0 < a₁ ∧ 0 < a₂ ∧
          (a₁ : ℝ) + a₂ > n + f r * Real.log n ∧
          a₁.factorial * a₂.factorial ∣
            n.factorial * (∏ i ∈ Finset.range r, Nat.nth Nat.Prime i) ^ n}.Infinite := by
  sorry

end Erdos401

reformulations.difference: The admissible n range over all naturals, including n = 0 where Lean defines Real.log 0 = 0, instead of restricting to the positive integers implicit in the source.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Deleting any finite initial segment does not change infinitude. For every predicate P on ℕ and N, {n | P n}.Infinite is equivalent to {n | N ≤ n ∧ P n}.Infinite. Applying this inside the quantifiers gives equivalence of the entire existence statement with its version restricted to n ≥ 2. Consequently, the small solutions at n = 0 and n = 1 do not weaken the problem.

sources_consulted: T. F. Bloom, Erdős Problem #401, https://www.erdosproblems.com/401 — read through https://web.archive.org/web/20260801000000id_/https://www.erdosproblems.com/401, including the quantifier discussion, alternative variant, and recorded solution.
Erdős–Graham, Old and New Problems and Results in Combinatorial Number Theory (1980), pp. 76–78, especially p. 78: https://mathweb.ucsd.edu/~ronspubs/80_11_number_theory.pdf

Factorial divisibility with bounded primes beyond the logarithmic barrier: an infinitely-many n result of Erdős type, Introduction, Theorem 1, Remark 1, and proof conclusion: https://drive.google.com/uc?export=download&id=1SY_LjPToevYaFl5eNl-rUxJrjrP5u4RC
Local Mathlib sources for Nat.nth, Nat.Prime, prime enumeration, Nat.factorial, Finset.range, Real.log, Set.Infinite, Filter.atTop, and Filter.Tendsto; FormalConjecturesUtil/Answer.lean.
review.notes: The sole theorem faithfully states the source's adopted infinitely-many-n interpretation, not the separately discussed and disproved all-large-n variant. Prime indexing, product powers, strict inequality, quantifier dependencies, and answer(True) all agree. The solved and Lean-verified status agrees with the archived source and current database. Sandbox checks in /workspace/review/scratch.lean verified boundary cases, prime-product positivity, and the relevant equivalences. /workspace/review/bridge.lean proves that the linked theorem's explicit function tends to infinity and that its conclusion implies this file's statement, without sorry-dependent axioms. The external artifact contains no explicit sorry or custom axioms; its full replay was not verified in its original Lean/Mathlib 4.29.1 environment, since the available 4.33.1 environment produces compatibility errors.
